findings.title: Zero-length date overrides are never recognized as such
findings.body: The code compares two newly-created Dayjs objects with `===`, which compares object identity and is always false even when `date.start` and `date.end` represent the same instant. Consequently, the special handling for a zero-length/full-day override never executes. Such an override can leave a slot at its boundary available instead of marking the host unavailable, allowing a booking during an intended day off. Compare the timestamps (for example with `isSame`) instead.

findings.title: Fixed-host working-hours validation ignores the event duration
findings.body: `end` is calculated from `slotStartTime` exactly as `start` is, so the condition only verifies that the slot starts before `workingHour.endTime`; it never verifies that the event ends before it. For round-robin events with a fixed host, a slot generated from a loose host's availability can therefore be retained even though the fixed host's shift ends partway through the event (for example, a 60-minute event starting at 09:30 with the fixed host available only until 10:00). The end value must include `eventLength` and be checked against the fixed host's availability.

findings.title: Multiple override windows on one day are treated as an intersection
findings.body: The `find` callback returns `true` when a slot is outside any individual override window, and the outer code immediately rejects the slot. If a host has two availability override ranges on the same date, a slot inside the first range is necessarily outside the second range and is rejected. This makes all slots unavailable whenever date overrides contain multiple separate windows, rather than accepting slots covered by at least one window. The logic should first collect the overrides for the date and accept a slot if it fits within any applicable override range.
